question.text: As per SEBI regulations, what is the status of nomination for single-holder mutual fund folios subscribed on or after September 30, 2023?

answer.text: Nomination is completely optional and the investor can leave the field blank
Nomination is mandatory and the investor must name at least one nominee
Nomination disclosure is mandatory — the investor must either nominate or explicitly opt out of nomination
Nomination is required only for investments exceeding Rs. 5 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: For investors subscribing on or after September 30, 2023, SEBI requires the investor to either provide nominee details or sign an explicit opt-out declaration. The investor cannot simply leave the nomination field blank — they must make and record a choice. The Trap: 'Mandatory disclosure' is different from 'mandatory nomination.' The investor is not forced to nominate; they are forced to make a choice and declare it. Note that the compulsory nomination/declaration provisions are optional for joint-holding folios, so the rule narrows to single-holder folios or subscribers covered by the rule. Note: Always encourage nomination — without a nominee, the family faces a lengthy legal process to claim the investments after the holder's death.
